security_audit.summary: The static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline code formatting. The system-reconnaissance findings are reflective checklist text, not host inspection. A medium semantic risk remains because the skill asks agents to edit files and commit changes by default.

remediation.suggestion: Add mandatory user confirmation before file writes and a separate confirmation before commits.
Require a user-approved target file list or restrict edits to documented RII paths.
Require a changed-file list and diff summary before finalizing the harvest.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Repository Modification and Commit Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs the agent to implement updates by default, edit each target file, create a PHR, and commit changes. This can persist broad repository changes without explicit confirmation for each write or commit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly tells the agent to make edits and commit changes by default. The risk is procedural and intent-level, not a static command-execution pattern.

content.user_title: Capture Session Learnings for Future Work
content.value_statement: Important session lessons are often lost after a task ends. This skill turns corrections and patterns into reusable project knowledge.
actual_capabilities: Identifies corrections, format drift, and repeated failure modes from a session.
Classifies learnings by target RII component, such as commands, agents, skills, or project guidance.
Provides structured templates for documenting each learning, placement, rationale, and source.
Guides agents through reading target files before preparing precise updates.
Defines validation checks for routing, duplicate detection, style matching, and final harvest summaries.
limitations: The skill depends on accurate session context from the user or agent.
It does not validate whether the target project uses the same RII structure.
It can propose broad edits unless users define boundaries first.
It requires human review before commits in sensitive repositories.

use_cases.title: Standardize Post-Session Learning Capture
use_cases.description: Turn corrections from a productive session into durable project guidance.

use_cases.title: Update Agent and Skill Instructions
use_cases.description: Route repeated agent mistakes to the right reusable instruction file.

use_cases.title: Keep Process Documentation Current
use_cases.description: Record new workflow rules where future sessions will find them.

prompt_templates.title: Harvest a Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Harvest learnings from this session. Identify corrections, classify each learning, and propose the target RII component before editing.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Correction
prompt_templates.prompt: We corrected a recurring format issue. Use the skill to document the root cause and show where the fix belongs.

prompt_templates.title: Update Reusable Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this session for reusable workflow patterns. Read the likely target files and prepare precise updates with rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Full Harvest
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a full session intelligence harvest. Before edits or commits, show the target files, proposed changes, validation checks, and confirmation points.

output_examples.input: A session fixed skill format drift across several instruction files.
output_examples.output: A harvest summary listing each learning, its target component, the applied update, and the validation result.

output_examples.input: A user asks what should be encoded after a workflow failure.
output_examples.output: A routed learning plan that names the root cause, target file, exact placement, and review steps.

output_examples.input: A team wants to preserve a new planning rule for future agents.
output_examples.output: A concise update proposal for the relevant agent or command guidance, with rationale and confirmation checkpoints.

best_practices: Ask for a dry-run summary before applying edits.
Review target files and diffs before any commit.
Use precise learning titles, root causes, and target components.
anti_patterns: Running harvests on vague or unresolved sessions.
Committing updates before reviewing the changed files.
Adding the same guidance to unrelated components.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after a session that corrected errors, found repeated patterns, or produced guidance worth reusing.

faq.question: Does it edit files automatically?
faq.answer: The source workflow encourages edits by default. Ask for confirmation gates before using it in important repositories.

faq.question: What are RII components?
faq.answer: They are reusable project knowledge files, such as agent instructions, commands, skills, and core guidance.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the correction made, the original mistake, likely root cause, and files or workflows affected.

faq.question: How do I reduce risk?
faq.answer: Request a dry run, approve target files, inspect diffs, and confirm separately before any commit.
